title.zh: 卷一百三十九 志1: 天文志
title.raw: 卷一百三十九 志1: 天文志 Volume 139: Treatises 1 Astronomy

sentences.zh: 天文志

translations.literal: Treatise on Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy Monograph

translations.literal: Opening section bracket 〈
translations.idiomatic: Opening section bracket 〈

sentences.zh: （案：《薛史天文志序》《永樂大典》原闕，然其日食、星變諸門，事跡具存，較《歐陽史·司天考》為詳備。

translations.literal: (Note: The preface to the Astronomy Treatise in the 《Xue History》 and in the 《Yongle Dadian》 are originally missing; however, the sections on solar eclipses, stellar transformations, and the like still preserve their records in full, and are more detailed and complete than the 《Examination of the Directors of Astronomy》 in Ouyang's History.)
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The preface to the Astronomy Treatise in the 《History of Xue Juzheng》 and the corresponding text in the 《Yongle Encyclopedia》 are lost in the sources, but the sections on solar eclipses, comets, and other celestial phenomena remain intact and are fuller than Ouyang Xiu's 《Directors of Astronomy》 monograph in the New History.)

sentences.zh: 今考《五代會要》所載星變、物異諸門，與《司天考》互有詳略。

translations.literal: Now examining the sections on stellar transformations and strange phenomena recorded in the 《Essentials of the Five Dynasties》, compared with the 《Examination of Directors of Astronomy》, each has parts more detailed and parts more abbreviated.
translations.idiomatic: A comparison of the stellar anomalies and prodigies recorded in the 《Essentials of the Five Dynasties》 with Ouyang's 《Examination of Directors of Astronomy》 shows that each source is fuller in some respects and scantier in others.

sentences.zh: 蓋五代典章散佚，各記所聞，未能畫一也。

translations.literal: This is because the statutes and regulations of the Five Dynasties were scattered and lost, and each record wrote what it heard, unable to be made uniform.
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of the Five Dynasties had largely disintegrated, so each compiler recorded what came to hand, and no single standard could be imposed.

sentences.zh: 參考諸書，當以《薛史》為得其實焉。）〉

translations.literal: Referencing the various books, one ought to take the 《Xue History》 as obtaining the reality.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When the various sources are weighed together, the 《History of Xue Juzheng》 should be regarded as closest to the facts.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁太祖乾化元年，正月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the first day of the first month (bingxu day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua (911), on New Year's Day of the first month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 時言事諸臣，多引漢高祖末年日蝕於歲首，太祖甚惡之，於是素服避正殿，百官各守本司。

translations.literal: At the time the various officials who spoke on affairs mostly cited the solar eclipse at the year's beginning in the final years of Emperor Gaozu of Han; the Taizu greatly detested this, and thereupon wore plain white garments and avoided the main hall, while the hundred officials each guarded their original departments.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists at court repeatedly cited how a solar eclipse at the year's opening had portended trouble in the last years of Han Gaozu's reign. Taizu was profoundly alarmed. He put on mourning dress, withdrew from the main audience hall, and ordered every ministry to maintain vigil at its post.

sentences.zh: 是日，有司奏：「雲初陰晦，事同不蝕。

translations.literal: That day, the responsible offices memorialized: "At first the clouds were dark and overcast, the matter being the same as no eclipse."
translations.idiomatic: That same day the responsible offices reported: "Thick cloud at first kept the sky dark, so that in effect no eclipse was visible."

sentences.zh: 」百僚奉表稱賀。

translations.literal: " The hundred officials presented memorials congratulating him.
translations.idiomatic: The entire bureaucracy submitted congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 末帝寵德三年，十月辛未朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongde of the Last Emperor, on the first day of the tenth month (xinwei day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongde (923), on the first day of the tenth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光三年，四月癸亥朔，時有司奏：「日蝕在卯，主歲大旱。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on the first day of the fourth month (guhai day), at the time the responsible offices memorialized: "The solar eclipse occurs in mao, presiding over a great drought for the year."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang (925), on the first day of the fourth month, the astronomical bureau reported: "The eclipse falls in the mao double-hour and portends a severe drought for the year."

sentences.zh: 明宗天成元年，八月乙酉朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong, on the first day of the eighth month (yiyou day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (926), on the first day of the eighth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二年，八月己卯朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eighth month (jimao day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (927), on the first day of the eighth month, the sun was eclipsed again.

sentences.zh: 三年，二月丁丑朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the second month (dingchou day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (928), on the first day of the second month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 其日陰雲不見，百官稱賀。

translations.literal: That day cloudy skies prevented sight of it, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud cover that day hid the phenomenon from view, and the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，六月癸巳朔，日蝕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, on the first day of the sixth month (guisi day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing (930), on the first day of the sixth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 其日陰冥不見，至夕大雨。

translations.literal: That day was dark and obscure without visibility, and by evening there was heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: The sky remained overcast and the eclipse could not be seen; heavy rain fell by evening.

sentences.zh: 二年，十一月甲申朔，先是，司天奏：「朔日合食二分，伏緣所蝕微少，太陽光影相鑠，伏恐不辨虧闕，請其日不入閣。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eleventh month (jiashen day), beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "On the new-moon day the eclipse should cover two parts in ten; it is submitted that because the portion eclipsed is very slight, the solar light and shadow will blend together, and it is submitted that one fears being unable to distinguish the waning and deficiency—request that on that day Your Majesty not enter the inner court."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (931), on the first day of the eleventh month, the astronomical bureau had earlier reported: "The eclipse on the new-moon day should cover two-tenths of the sun's disk, but because the obscuration will be slight, sunlight and shadow may merge and the loss may be hard to discern. We request that Your Majesty not hold court in the inner palace that day."

sentences.zh: 百官守司。

translations.literal: The hundred officials shall guard their departments.
translations.idiomatic: All officials should remain at their posts.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖天福二年，正月乙卯，先是，司天奏：「正月二日，太陽虧蝕，宜避正殿，開諸營門，蓋藏兵器，半月不宜用軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, on the second day of the first month (yimao day), beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "On the second day of the first month the sun will suffer eclipse; it is fitting to avoid the main hall, open the gates of the various camps, cover and store weapons, and for half a month it is not fitting to use the army."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu (937), on the second day of the first month, the astronomical bureau had reported in advance: "On the second day of the first month the sun will be eclipsed. Your Majesty should withdraw from the main hall, open the gates of every camp, put away weapons, and refrain from military operations for half a month."

sentences.zh: 」是日太陽虧，十分內食三分，在尾宿十七度。

translations.literal: " That day the sun was deficient; within ten parts, three parts were eaten, in the seventeenth degree of the Tail constellation.
translations.idiomatic: On that day the sun was eclipsed: three-tenths of the disk was obscured, in the seventeenth degree of the Tail lodge.

sentences.zh: 日出東方，以帶蝕三分，漸生，至卯時復滿。

translations.literal: The sun rose in the east with a belt-like eclipse of three parts, gradually regenerating, and by the mao double-hour was full again.
translations.idiomatic: The sun rose in the east with a belt-shaped eclipse covering three-tenths of the disk; it gradually recovered, and by the mao hour was whole again.

sentences.zh: 三年，正月戊申朔，司天先奏，其日日蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the first month (wushen day), the Directorate of Astronomy had memorialized in advance that on that day the sun would be eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (938), on New Year's Day, the astronomical bureau had predicted a solar eclipse for that day.

sentences.zh: 至是日不蝕，內外稱賀。

translations.literal: When that day came there was no eclipse, and within and without offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the day arrived, no eclipse occurred, and court and capital alike offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 四年，七月庚子朔，時中書門下奏：「謹按舊禮：日有變，天子素服避正殿，太史以所司救日於社，陳五兵、五鼓、五麾，東戟西矛，南弩北楯，中央置鼓，服從其位，百職廢務，素服守司，重列於庭，每等異位，向日而立，明復而止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the first day of the seventh month (gengzi day), at the time the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Respectfully according to the old rites: when the sun has a transformation, the Son of Heaven wears plain garments and avoids the main hall; the Grand Astrologer with his office performs the rite of rescuing the sun at the altar of soil, displaying five weapons, five drums, and five banners—halberds to the east, spears to the west, crossbows to the south, shields to the north, with a drum placed in the center; garments follow their positions; the hundred offices suspend duties, wear plain garments and guard their departments, arrayed in ranks in the courtyard, each grade in a different position, standing facing the sun until brightness is restored, then stopping."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (939), on the first day of the seventh month, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: "According to the ancient rites, when the sun shows an anomaly the Son of Heaven puts on white garments and withdraws from the main hall; the Grand Astrologer performs the rite of rescuing the sun at the altar of soil, displaying five weapons, five drums, and five banners—halberds to the east, spears to the west, crossbows to the south, shields to the north, with a drum at the center. Officials take their stations in plain dress; all duties are suspended while each office keeps watch; ranks stand in the courtyard by grade, facing the sun until the light returns, and only then disperse."

sentences.zh: 今所司法物，鹹不能具，去歲正旦日食，唯謹藏兵仗，皇帝避正殿素食，百官守司。

translations.literal: Now the ritual objects in the charge of the offices all cannot be fully provided; last year at the New Year there was a solar eclipse, and only weapons were carefully stored, the emperor avoided the main hall and ate vegetarian food, and the hundred officials guarded their departments.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual implements now in the keeping of the offices cannot all be supplied. At last year's New Year eclipse we could only store away weapons, have the emperor withdraw to the main hall on a vegetarian diet, and keep officials at their posts."

sentences.zh: 今且欲依近禮施行。

translations.literal: Now we wish for the time being to carry out according to the recent rites.
translations.idiomatic: We propose to follow the simplified recent practice on this occasion.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，四月甲寅朔，是日百官守司，太陽不蝕，上表稱賀。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, on the first day of the fourth month (jiayin day), that day the hundred officials guarded their departments; the sun was not eclipsed, and memorials were submitted offering congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year (942), on the first day of the fourth month, officials remained at their posts as ordered; the sun was not eclipsed, and congratulatory memorials were submitted.

sentences.zh: 八年，四月戊申朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on the first day of the fourth month (wushen day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (943), on the first day of the fourth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 少帝開運元年，九月庚午朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyun of the Young Emperor, on the first day of the ninth month (gengwu day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaiyun (944), on the first day of the ninth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 二年，八月甲子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the first day of the eighth month (jiazi day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (945), on the first day of the eighth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 三年，二月壬戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the first day of the second month (renxu day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (946), on the first day of the second month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝乾祐三年，十一月甲子朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qianyou of Emperor Yindi of Han, on the first day of the eleventh month (jiazi day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qianyou (950), on the first day of the eleventh month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 周太祖廣順二年，四月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the first day of the fourth month (bingxu day), the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun (952), on the first day of the fourth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 月食

translations.literal: Lunar Eclipses.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Eclipses

sentences.zh: 梁太祖開平四年，十二月十四日夜，先是，司天奏：「是日月蝕，不宜用兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, beforehand the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "On that day the moon will be eclipsed; it is not fitting to use the army."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiping (910), on the night of the fourteenth day of the twelfth month, the astronomical bureau had reported in advance: "A lunar eclipse is due that night; military operations should be avoided."

sentences.zh: 」時王景仁方總大軍北伐，追之不及。

translations.literal: " At the time Wang Jingren was just then commanding the great army on a northern campaign; pursuing the order, they did not reach it in time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingren was then leading the main army on a northern campaign, and the recall could not overtake him in time.

sentences.zh: 至五年正月二日，果為後唐莊宗大敗於柏鄉。

translations.literal: By the second day of the first month of the fifth year, he was indeed greatly defeated by Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang at Boxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day of the first month of the fifth year (911), he suffered a crushing defeat from Later Tang's Zhuangzong at Boxiang.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光三年，三月戊申，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on the day wushen of the third month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang (925), on the wushen day of the third month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 九月甲辰，月蝕。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen of the ninth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen day of the ninth month, the moon was eclipsed again.

sentences.zh: 明宗天成三年，十二月乙卯，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong, on the day yimao of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng (928), on the yimao day of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 四年，六月癸丑望，月食。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the full moon of the sixth month (guichou day), the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (929), at the full moon of the sixth month, there was a lunar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚戌，月蝕。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu day of the twelfth month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 周世宗顯德三年，正月戊申，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Shizong of Zhou, on the day wushen of the first month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande (956), on the wushen day of the first month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 五年，十一月辛未，月蝕。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on the day xinwei of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year (958), on the xinwei day of the eleventh month, the moon was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: ◎月暈

translations.literal: ◎ Lunar Halos.
translations.idiomatic: Lunar Halos

sentences.zh: 唐明宗天成元年，十一月，月暈匝火、木。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, in the eleventh month, the moon was haloed, encircled by Fire and Wood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng (926), in the eleventh month, a halo ringed the moon, with the planets Fire and Wood completing the circle.

sentences.zh: ◎彗孛梁太祖乾化二年，四月甲戌夜，彗見於靈臺之西。

translations.literal: ◎ Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the night of the day jiaxu of the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Comets and Broom Stars. In the second year of Qianhua (912), on the night of the jiaxu day of the fourth month, a comet appeared west of the Observatory Terrace.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗天成三年，十月庚午夜，西南有孛，長丈餘，東南指，在牛宿五度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, on the night of the day gengwu of the tenth month, in the southwest there was a broom star, more than a zhang in length, pointing southeast, in the fifth degree of the Ox constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tiancheng (928), on the night of the gengwu day of the tenth month, a broom star more than ten feet long appeared in the southwest, its tail pointing southeast, in the fifth degree of the Ox lodge.

sentences.zh: 末帝清泰三年，九月己丑，彗出虛、危，長尺餘，形細微，經天壘、哭星。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingtai of the Last Emperor, on the day jichou of the ninth month, a comet issued from Emptiness and Rooftop, more than a chi in length, its form slight and fine, passing through the Celestial Ramparts and Wailing stars.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Qingtai (936), on the jichou day of the ninth month, a comet emerged between the Emptiness and Rooftop lodges. It was just over a foot long and faint in appearance, and passed through the Celestial Ramparts and the Wailing Star.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖天福六年，九月，有彗星長丈餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu of Emperor Gaozu of Jin, in the ninth month, there was a comet more than a zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu (941), in the ninth month, a comet more than ten feet long was observed.

sentences.zh: 八年，十月庚戌夜，有彗見於東方，西指，尾長一丈，在角九度。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, on the night of the day gengxu of the tenth month, a comet was seen in the east, pointing west, its tail one zhang in length, in the ninth degree of the Horn constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year (943), on the night of the gengxu day of the tenth month, a comet appeared in the east with its tail pointing west; the tail was ten feet long, in the ninth degree of the Horn lodge.

sentences.zh: 周太祖顯德三年，正月壬戌夜，有星孛於參角，其芒指於東南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Emperor Taizu of Zhou, on the night of the day renxu of the first month, there was a broom star at the horn of the Three Stars constellation, its rays pointing toward the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande (956), on the night of the renxu day of the first month, a broom star appeared at the horn of the Three Stars lodge, its rays pointing southeast.

sentences.zh: ◎五星淩犯梁太祖開平二年，正月乙亥，歲星犯月。

translations.literal: ◎ Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping of Emperor Taizu of Liang, on the day yihai of the first month, the Year Star encroached upon the moon.
translations.idiomatic: Encroachments of the Five Planets. In the second year of Kaiping (908), on the yihai day of the first month, Jupiter encroached upon the moon.

sentences.zh: 乾化二年，五月壬戌，熒惑犯心大星，去心四度，順行。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianhua, on the day renxu of the fifth month, the Sparkling Deluder encroached upon the great star of the Heart constellation, four degrees from the Heart, moving in direct motion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianhua (912), on the renxu day of the fifth month, Mars encroached upon the principal star of the Heart lodge, four degrees from the Heart, in direct motion.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「心為帝王之星。

translations.literal: The prognostication says: "The Heart is the star of the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication reads: "The Heart is the star of the sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」其年六月五日，帝崩。

translations.literal: " In that year on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光二年，八月戊子，熒惑犯星。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongguang of Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang, on the day wuzi of the eighth month, the Sparkling Deluder encroached upon the Star constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongguang (924), on the wuzi day of the eighth month, Mars encroached upon the Star lodge.

sentences.zh: 三年，三月丙申，熒惑犯上相。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the day bingshen of the third month, the Sparkling Deluder encroached upon the Upper Minister star.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year (925), on the bingshen day of the third month, Mars encroached upon the Upper Minister star.

sentences.zh: 四月甲申，熒惑犯左執法。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the fourth month, the Sparkling Deluder encroached upon the Left Law Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day of the fourth month, Mars encroached upon the Left Law Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 六月丙寅，歲犯右執法。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin of the sixth month, the Year Star encroached upon the Right Law Enforcer.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day of the sixth month, Jupiter encroached upon the Right Law Enforcer.

sentences.zh: 九月己亥，熒惑在江東犯第一星。

translations.literal: On the day jihai of the ninth month, the Sparkling Deluder in the east of the river encroached upon the first star.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day of the ninth month, Mars, east of the river, encroached upon the first star.

translations.literal: Opening section bracket 〈
translations.idiomatic: Opening section bracket 〈

sentences.zh: （案《歐陽史》：九月丙辰，太白、歲相犯。

translations.literal: (Note: The 《Ouyang History》 records: On the day bingchen of the ninth month, the Great White and the Year Star mutually encroached.
translations.idiomatic: (Note: The 《Ouyang History》 records that on the bingchen day of the ninth month, Venus and Jupiter mutually encroached.

translations.idiomatic: From the jichou day of the eighth month in the first year, Saturn had entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure, encroaching upon the Upper General, the Left and Right Law Enforcers, the Inner Screen, and the Usher stars, tracing hooked paths back and forth for four hundred forty-three days before emerging from the left side gate.

sentences.zh: 先是，熒惑勾己於房、心間，凡數月，至是與心大星合度，是夜順行。

translations.literal: Before this, the Sparkling Deluder had moved in hooked curves between the Room and Heart constellations for several months; reaching this point it shared the degree with the great star of the Heart, and that night moved in direct motion.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，五月己未，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, on the day jiwei of the fifth month, the Great White was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, on the jiwei day of the fifth month, Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 漢天福十三年，四月丙子，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianfu of Han, on the day bingzi of the fourth month, the Great White was seen by day.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianfu, on the bingzi day of the fourth month, Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年，四月壬午，太白晝見，

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou, on the day renwu of the fourth month, the Great White was seen by day,
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou, on the renwu day of the fourth month, Venus was visible in daylight,

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，二月庚寅，太白經天。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, on the day gengyin of the second month, the Great White crossed the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun, on the gengyin day of the second month, Venus crossed the meridian at noon.

sentences.zh: ◎流星

translations.literal: ◎ Shooting Stars.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting Stars

sentences.zh: 梁乾化元年，十一月甲辰，東方有流星如數升器，出畢宿口，曳光三丈餘，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianhua of Liang, on the day jiachen of the eleventh month, in the east there was a shooting star like a vessel of several sheng, issuing from the mouth of the Net constellation, trailing light for more than three zhang, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianhua, on the jiachen day of the eleventh month, a shooting star the size of a multi-pint vessel appeared in the east, emerging from the mouth of the Net lodge and trailing light for more than thirty feet, with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 唐長興二年，九月丙戌夜，二鼓初，東北方有小流星入北斗魁滅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing of Tang, on the night of the day bingxu of the ninth month, at the beginning of the second drum, in the northeast there was a small shooting star that entered the leader of the Northern Dipper and was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing, on the night of the bingxu day of the ninth month, at the second watch, a small meteor in the northeast entered the leader of the Northern Dipper and vanished.

sentences.zh: 至五鼓初，西北方次北有流星，狀如半升器，初小後大，速流如奎滅。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the fifth drum, in the northwest slightly north there was a shooting star, shaped like a half-sheng vessel, at first small then large, streaming swiftly like Kui and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch, a meteor slightly north of northwest appeared, shaped like a half-pint vessel, growing from small to large as it streaked swiftly past the Striding Legs lodge and vanished.

sentences.zh: 尾跡凝天，屈曲似雲而散，光明燭地。

translations.literal: Its tail-trail congealed in the sky, bending and twisting like clouds as it dispersed, its brilliance illuminating the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Its trail congealed across the sky, curling like clouds before dispersing, its brilliance lighting the ground.

sentences.zh: 又東北有流星如大桃，出下臺星，西北速流，至斗柄第三星旁滅。

translations.literal: Again in the northeast there was a shooting star like a large peach, issuing from the Lower Terrace star, streaming swiftly northwest, and extinguished beside the third star of the Dipper's handle.
translations.idiomatic: Another meteor the size of a large peach appeared in the northeast, emerging from the Lower Terrace star and streaking northwest until it vanished beside the third star of the Dipper's handle.

sentences.zh: 五鼓後至明，中天及四方有小流星百餘，流註交橫。

translations.literal: From after the fifth drum until dawn, at the center of heaven and in the four directions there were more than a hundred small shooting stars, streaming and crossing one another.
translations.idiomatic: From after the fifth watch until dawn, more than a hundred small meteors crossed the zenith and the four quarters of the sky, their paths intersecting.

sentences.zh: 應順元年春，二月辛未夜，有大星如五升器，流於東北，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yingshun, on the night of the day xinwei of the second month, there was a great star like a five-sheng vessel, streaming toward the northeast, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yingshun, on the night of the xinwei day of the second month, a great meteor the size of a five-pint vessel streaked toward the northeast with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，九月辛丑夜，五鼓初，有大星如五斗器而南流，尾跡長數丈，亦赤色，移時盤屈如龍形，蹙縮如二鏵，相鬥而散。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai, on the night of the day xinchou of the ninth month, at the beginning of the fifth drum, there was a great star like a five-dou vessel streaming southward, its tail-trail several zhang in length and also red in color; after a time it coiled and bent like a dragon's form, contracting like two plowshares fighting each other, then dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qingtai, on the night of the xinchou day of the ninth month, at the fifth watch, a great meteor the size of a five-peck vessel streamed southward, its red trail several yards long. After a time it coiled like a dragon, then contracted as if two plowshares were clashing before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 又一星稍小，東流，有尾跡，凝成白氣，食頃方散。

translations.literal: Again one star slightly smaller streamed eastward, with a tail-trail that congealed into white vapor and only dispersed after the time of a meal.
translations.idiomatic: A somewhat smaller star followed, streaming eastward with a trail that congealed into white vapor and took the space of a meal to dissipate.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，三月壬申夜，四鼓後，東方有大流星，狀如三升器，其色白，長尺餘，屈曲流出河鼓星東三尺，流丈餘滅。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu of Jin, on the night of the day renshen of the third month, after the fourth drum, in the east there was a great shooting star, shaped like a three-sheng vessel, white in color, more than a chi in length, bending and twisting as it issued three chi east of the River Drum star, streaming for more than a zhang before extinguishing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu, on the night of the renshen day of the third month, after the fourth watch, a great meteor the size of a three-pint vessel appeared in the east, white and more than a foot long. It twisted as it emerged three feet east of the River Drum star, streaked for more than ten feet, and vanished.

sentences.zh: ◎雲氣

translations.literal: ◎ Cloud Vapors.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud Vapors

sentences.zh: 梁開平二年，三月丁丑夜，月有蒼白暈，又有白氣如人形十餘，皆東向，出於暈內。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping of Liang, on the night of the day dingchou of the third month, the moon had a pale blue halo, and again there were more than ten white vapors shaped like human forms, all facing east, issuing from within the halo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiping, on the night of the dingchou day of the third month, the moon showed a pale blue halo, and more than ten white vapors shaped like human figures, all facing east, emerged from within the halo.

sentences.zh: 九月乙酉，平旦，西方有氣如人形甚眾，皆若俯伏之狀，經刻乃散。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou of the ninth month, at dawn, in the west there were vapors like human forms in great number, all as if in prostrate posture; after the space of a quarter-hour they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyou day of the ninth month, at dawn, a multitude of vapors in human shape appeared in the west, all seeming to prostrate themselves; after a quarter-hour they dispersed.

sentences.zh: 唐同光三年，日有背氣，凡十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang of Tang, the sun had opposing vapors, twelve in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang, opposing solar vapors appeared twelve times.

sentences.zh: 三年，九月丁未夜，遍天陰雲，北方有聲如雷，四面雞雉皆雊，俗謂之「天狗落」。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the night of the day dingwei of the ninth month, clouds covered the entire sky; in the north there was a sound like thunder, and on all four sides chickens and pheasants all crowed; popularly it was called "the celestial dog falling."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on the night of the dingwei day of the ninth month, cloud covered the entire sky. Thunder sounded in the north, and chickens and pheasants crowed on every side; the people called it "the celestial dog falling."

sentences.zh: 是歲，日有背氣，凡十三。

translations.literal: That year, the sun had opposing vapors, thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year opposing solar vapors appeared thirteen times.

sentences.zh: 是月，司天監奏：「自七月三日陰雲大雨，至九月十八日後方晴，三辰行度災祥，數日不見。

translations.literal: That month, the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "From the third day of the seventh month cloudy skies and heavy rain, until after the eighteenth day of the ninth month it finally cleared; the movements and degrees of the three luminaries and their omens of disaster and blessing could not be seen for several days."
translations.idiomatic: That month the astronomical directorate reported: "From the third day of the seventh month until after the eighteenth day of the ninth month, cloud and heavy rain hid the sky. For several days the movements of the sun, moon, and stars and their omens could not be observed."

sentences.zh: 」閏十二月庚午，日有黑氣，似日，交相錯磨，測在室十度。

translations.literal: " In the intercalary twelfth month, on the day gengwu, the sun had black vapor resembling the sun, crossing and grinding against each other; measurement placed it in the tenth degree of the House constellation.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the intercalary twelfth month, black vapor resembling a second sun crossed and ground against the true sun; observation placed the phenomenon in the tenth degree of the House lodge.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，十二月壬辰，西方有赤氣，如火焰焰，約二千里。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, on the day renchen of the twelfth month, in the west there was red vapor, like blazing flames, extending about two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng, on the renchen day of the twelfth month, red vapor like blazing flame stretched across the west for roughly two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 占者云「不出二年，其下當有大兵。」

translations.literal: The diviner said: "Within two years, below it there should be great armies."
translations.idiomatic: Diviners declared: "Within two years great armies will arise in the region below."

sentences.zh: 長興三年，六月，司天監奏：「自月初至月終，每夜陰雲蔽天，不辨星月。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changxing, in the sixth month, the Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "From the beginning of the month to the end of the month, every night cloudy skies covered heaven, unable to distinguish stars and moon."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changxing, in the sixth month, the astronomical directorate reported: "From the first to the last night of the month, cloud covered the sky each night so that stars and moon could not be distinguished."

sentences.zh: 」應順元年，四月九日，白虹貫日，是時閔帝遇害。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yingshun, on the ninth day of the fourth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun; at that time Emperor Min was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yingshun, on the ninth day of the fourth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun; at that time Emperor Min was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，高祖將建義於太原，日傍多有五色雲，如蓮芰之狀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu of Jin, when the Gaozu was about to raise righteousness at Taiyuan, beside the sun there were many five-colored clouds, shaped like lotus seedpods.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, as Gaozu prepared to raise his banner at Taiyuan, many-colored clouds like lotus seedpods gathered beside the sun.

sentences.zh: 二年，正月丙辰，一鼓初，北方有赤氣，向西至戌亥地，東北至醜地已來向北，闊三丈餘，狀如火光。

translations.literal: In the second year, on the day bingchen of the first month, at the beginning of the first drum, in the north there was red vapor, extending west to the xu and hai regions, from the northeast to the chou region coming northward, three zhang and more in breadth, shaped like firelight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, on the bingchen day of the first month, at the first watch, red vapor in the north stretched west toward the xu and hai quarters and from the northeast through the chou quarter northward, more than thirty feet wide and shaped like firelight.

sentences.zh: 赤氣內見紫微宮共北斗諸星，其氣乍明乍暗。

translations.literal: Within the red vapor could be seen the Purple Forbidden Palace together with the stars of the Northern Dipper; the vapor was now bright, now dark.
translations.idiomatic: Within the red vapor the Purple Forbidden Palace and the stars of the Northern Dipper could be seen, the vapor flickering bright and dim.

sentences.zh: 至三點後，後有白氣數條，相次西行，直至三鼓後散。

translations.literal: By after the third point, afterward there were several streaks of white vapor, successively streaming westward, until after the third drum they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After the third hour, several streaks of white vapor followed one another westward until they dispersed after the third watch.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年十二月，日暈三重，上有背氣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, the sun had a triple halo, with opposing vapor above.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianyou, the sun showed a triple halo with opposing vapor above it.

sentences.zh: 周顯德三年，十二月庚午，白虹貫日，氣暈勾環。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande of Zhou, on the day gengwu of the twelfth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun, and vaporous halos hooked and encircled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande, on the gengwu day of the twelfth month, a white rainbow pierced the sun, with hooked and encircling vaporous halos.
